page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration provides 24.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The CPU includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI for vector neural network instructions) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results place the ecs.c7.3xlarge consistently in the average tier for its hardware class. Single-core performance is highlighted by a stress-ng score of 1874.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1531.0, while multi-core execution scales to a stress-ng score of 11644.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7760.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a high cached read speed of 633.64 GB/sec for small blocks, which drops to 76.48 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 46.87 GB/sec. In application-specific workloads, the instance achieves 11.74 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a static web serving throughput of 15.7 GB/sec.

Given its compute-heavy 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring sustained CPU performance without massive memory footprints. It is suitable for tasks like software compilation, where it scores 11558.0 on Geekbench Clang compilation, and multi-threaded decompression. However, its memory constraints and lack of GPU acceleration make it weak for larger AI tasks, as demonstrated by a weak prompt processing speed of 23.52 tokens/sec on a 7B LLM model. Appropriate workloads include web serving, intermediate database operations, and general-purpose compute tasks.

Built on a KVM hypervisor, it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators but offers an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. With a 2.0 GB per vCPU memory ratio, the instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is appropriate for web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate database operations.
